Subject: Discovery Recap: Inference Cost Pressure & Next Steps

Hi Amit / Priya —

Thanks for the time this morning — good conversation and I wanted to capture the key takeaways and proposed next steps so we have alignment. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary of pain points and goals (what you told us):
- Unit economics: Current serving costs are ~ $0.0035 per token on your self-hosted fleet; CFO target is ~ $0.0009/token at scale for the recommendation flows.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 200ms for 1k token-ish prompts; p50 ~ 80–120ms is fine.
- Throughput: burst to ~150 req/s, steady-state 60–80 req/s for the recommendation model.
- Quality constraints: open to INT8 quantization if we can validate <1% top-1 metric degradation on your eval set.
- Architecture: currently running a mix of NVIDIA A10s on AWS with in-house batching; limited prefix KV caching; no model-variant routing in prod.

Success criteria for a pilot (what success looks like to you):
1) Demonstrate 40–60% reduction in effective per-token cost at target latency (p95 <= 200ms) for a 2-week PoC.
2) No more than 1% drop on your offline NDCG metric when using quantized models.
3) Integration path for routing and KV caching with minimal infra changes (we demo a config-first approach).

Our immediate recommendations (initial scope for PoC):
- Start with a small dedicated pool (Redwood Dedicated) using a quantized variant of the model you specified. Rishi (cc'd) will recommend quantization and batching settings.
- Enable prefix KV caching for hot prompts to reduce token compute on steady-state flows.
- Run an A/B vs your current fleet across a mirrored traffic slice (5–10%) to measure unit economics and quality.

Attachments: I've attached the architecture notes you shared and our initial MAB cost estimates stubbed out for the demo.
(Attachment stubs: finbot-prod-arch-diagram.pdf; mab-estimates.xlsx)

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) Rishi to send a 1-page PoC plan and quantization recommendations — by Mon 3/23 EOD.
2) Quick technical sync (30 min) to align on deployment details — Tue 3/24 10:00am PT (please confirm).
3) PoC kickoff (provisioned dedicated pool + baseline run) — week of 3/30.

Can you confirm the 3 items above and the Tuesday 10am slot? If that works I'll send a calendar invite and loop in your infra lead for the technical sync.

Thanks again — excited to see if we can hit the unit economics target with a small pilot.

Best,

Marissa / team — quick followup from the SE side.

High-level PoC approach I'll include in Monday's doc (short bullets):
- Quantization: start with dynamic INT8 for encoder/decoder weights + post-training calibration on their eval set. If we see >0.7% degradation, fallback to mixed FP16/INT8 for sensitive layers.
- Batching: adaptive batching with a 25–50ms batching window for non-latency-critical endpoints; keep lower-latency endpoints in a low-latency routing tier. This should improve throughput with minimal p95 impact.
- Caching: enable prefix KV caching for the top ~15% of prompts (we'll identify these from their logs). Expect 10–25% fewer compute tokens depending on prompt locality.
- Rollback/guardrails: we'll instrument model-level canary with metric gates (NDCG, latency, error-rate) and an automatic rollback policy if gates fail. Also recommend a manual kill-switch for live traffic routing.

I'll send the 1-page PoC and proposed resource config by EOD Mon 3/23.
